title: RootCandidate comparison may behave unexpectedly with NaN RF metrics
description:
File: rust/lichen-rpl/src/multi_instance.rs
Lines: 762-768

The Ord implementation for RootCandidate compares combined_score() (f32) values:

```rust
.then_with(|| {
    other
        .combined_score()
        .partial_cmp(&self.combined_score())
        .unwrap_or(Ordering::Equal)
})
```

While unwrap_or(Equal) prevents panics on NaN comparison, it makes NaN-containing candidates compare Equal to all others, potentially selecting an invalid candidate if NaN propagates into rssi_ema or snr_ema.

Trigger: A sensor or parsing bug sets rssi_ema to f32::NAN. This candidate compares Equal on the RF metric axis, falling through to IID tiebreaker.

Bad behavior: A candidate with corrupted RF metrics could be selected over better candidates, or cause non-deterministic ordering.

Fix: Filter out candidates with non-finite RF metrics before comparison, or treat NaN as worst-case value (-Infinity).
close_reason: Already implemented. The RootCandidate comparison handles NaN RF metrics via: (1) input sanitization in with_rf_metrics/with_rssi_ema/with_snr_ema that replaces NaN with worst-case defaults, (2) total_cmp() at line 977 for Ord compliance, and (3) comprehensive tests at lines 2271-2300 verifying NaN sanitization and sorting behavior.
